## MEMORY EVIDENCE

---

[architecture_note | sources: planning/book-architecture.md | item mb-arch-q6-open]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z; DERIVED-LICENCE open-loop loop-q6]
Question 6 remains the largest unanswered part of the architecture. Chapters 4 to 9 enrich what the system can know about history; none of them has yet been asked whether that enrichment produces a better working context than query-only retrieval at the same budget. The planning notes list importance and retrieval policy, and context assembly under a fixed token budget, as candidate mechanisms rather than chapter commitments.

---

[open_loop | sources: content/books/memory/10-chapter.md | item mb-loop-ch10-experiment]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z; DERIVED-LICENCE open-loop loop-ch10-experiment]
Open: Chapter 10 carries an experiment-pending marker and no committed run. Until an E-10 run exists, the chapter states a hypothesis the book's own evidence discipline forbids presenting as a result.

---

[method_rule | sources: spec/benchmark-v0.1.md | item mb-method-baseline-rule]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Required baselines for any experiment: no memory, lexical retrieval, embedding top-k, embedding plus reranking, the current best system before the mechanism under test, the candidate system, and an ablation with the mechanism neutralised. A mechanism is not earned merely because an aggregate score rises; its intended failure class must improve without unacceptable regressions elsewhere.

---

[method_rule | sources: AGENTS.md, planning/book-architecture.md | item mb-method-earn]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
A mechanism enters the book only when a controlled experiment shows it beating the strongest conventional alternative on the failure class it claims to fix. Taxonomy does not earn a chapter; measured failure does. Every new layer is compared against the Chapter 3 retrieval baseline at a matched context budget, with the reader model and corpus held fixed.

---

[method_rule | sources: AGENTS.md | item mb-method-evidence-discipline]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Three evidence categories are never mixed: established background, book hypothesis, and book result. A pending experiment's outcome is never stated as fact, including in chapter openings that recap earlier chapters. A fluent summary of retrieved text is not remembering; behaviour change is the test.

---

[experiment_result | sources: experiments/benchmark/runs/ch9-20260920T000629Z-open-loops/results.json | item mb-refutes-ch9-scope]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z; DISPUTES fellow-group claim (unresolved)]
[disagrees with: mb-ch09-result]
Dissenting note retained: the Chapter 9 status accuracy of 1.0 holds on fixture-level cases with oracle-labelled expectations, so it does not establish that expectation extraction from raw history would reach the same accuracy. The verdict is fixture-level, and the chapter says so.

## MEMORY EVIDENCE

[implementation_detail | sources: cocoder/context/build.py | item cc-context-window]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
CoCoder builds the model's context from the open file, the symbols it references, recent diffs and the failing test output, under a fixed token budget. Selection is by static reference graph first and embedding similarity second.

---

[experiment_result | sources: cocoder/eval/harness.md | item cc-eval-harness]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
CoCoder's evaluation harness measures patch acceptance rate, test-pass rate and token cost per task, with a distraction column counting admitted context that no accepted patch referenced.

---

[method_rule | sources: cocoder/docs/policy.md | item cc-evidence-refs]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
CoCoder requires that every suggested edit name the files and symbols that justified it, so a wrong suggestion can be traced to the context that produced it rather than to the model alone.

---

[implementation_detail | sources: cocoder/memory/notes.py | item cc-memory-notes]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
CoCoder stores per-repository memory notes: conventions, build commands, and corrections the user has made before, retrieved whenever a new task starts in that repository.

---

[planning_note | sources: cocoder/docs/roadmap.md | item cc-improve-context]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Planned improvement to CoCoder's context system: drop whole-file inclusion in favour of symbol slices, and measure whether the freed budget improves patch acceptance.

[architecture_note | sources: planning/book-architecture.md | item mb-arch-q6-open]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z; DERIVED-LICENCE open-loop loop-q6]
Question 6 remains the largest unanswered part of the architecture. Chapters 4 to 9 enrich what the system can know about history; none of them has yet been asked whether that enrichment produces a better working context than query-only retrieval at the same budget. The planning notes list importance and retrieval policy, and context assembly under a fixed token budget, as candidate mechanisms rather than chapter commitments.

---

[implementation_detail | sources: solution/graph_memory | item mb-impl-graphrag]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Chapter 4 indexing runs graphrag 3.1.2 inside solution/.venv, with Basic, Local, Global and DRIFT query modes exercised through the chapter runner rather than through unit tests. Index builds require Ollama for extraction and take minutes, not seconds.

---

[implementation_detail | sources: solution/memory_baseline/storage.py | item mb-impl-postgres]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
The baseline store runs PostgreSQL with pgvector on port 5434 via docker compose, with an HNSW index and a tsvector column for full-text search. Lexical search uses OR-of-terms with ts_rank_cd ordering because plain AND matching retrieves nothing for ordinary question phrasing.

---

[implementation_detail | sources: solution/temporal_memory/transport.py | item mb-impl-zeromq]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
The Chapter 8 transport uses ZeroMQ PUSH/PULL with an append-only log behind it. ZeroMQ is transport, never the store: the log is canonical and projections rebuild from it. The demo binds an inproc socket, replays the frozen event file and asserts the rebuilt projection digest matches.

---

[experiment_result | sources: content/books/memory/06-chapter.md, experiments/benchmark/runs/ch6-20260919-nexus | item mb-ch06-result]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
The Chapter 6 Nexus earned a governance role rather than a quality role: routing across memory mechanisms did not by itself improve answers, but it made the choice of mechanism explicit and auditable. That outcome is the book's precedent for accepting a mechanism on control grounds when the quality delta is absent.

---

[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]

---

[implementation_detail | sources: writer/context/runtime.py | item wr-context-runtime]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Writer's context runtime assembles a request from candidates under a budget and emits a bundle with a trace. The vocabulary is deliberately similar to the memory programme's: requests, candidates, budgets, policies, bundles and traces all appear in the module names.

---

[experiment_result | sources: writer/eval/retrieval.md | item wr-retrieval-eval]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Writer's retrieval evaluation measures context precision and recall against a hand-labelled set of source passages per section, with a separate token-cost column. The harness reports per-section results before any aggregate.

---

[implementation_detail | sources: writer/memory/store.py | item wr-memory-store]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Writer keeps a per-document memory store of prior drafts, editorial notes and style decisions, retrieved by embedding similarity when a new section is drafted.

---

[planning_note | sources: writer/docs/roadmap.md | item wr-improve-context]
[CURRENT as of 2026-09-20T12:00:00Z]
Planned improvement to Writer's context system: cache embeddings per document version, raise the candidate pool, and add a redundancy penalty so near-duplicate draft fragments stop occupying the budget.
